title: Imported term text in any capitals or spacing saves in the term's spelling
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, working in {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The shop's own term {Term-A}, named "Net 10", is active.
    For example: {Term-A} is Net 10.
  • A contacts import file with three new customers: {Customer-A} with the credit term "net 10", {Customer-B} with "NET10" and {Customer-C} with "Net 10".
    For example: they are ZZAUTOTEST S10-02 Alpha, Bravo and Charlie.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Import the file through Settings, Data Import, Contacts.
  2. Open {Customer-A}'s customer page.
  3. Open {Customer-B}'s customer page.
  4. Open {Customer-C}'s customer page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the import finishes; no row is refused because of its credit term.
  • Step 2: the "Credit term" reads "Net 10" (the term's own spelling).
  • Step 3: it reads "Net 10".
  • Step 4: it reads "Net 10".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11679 (Story 10, Imports and Public API)

  • S10-R3: “A credit term that matches one of the shop's terms (standard or its own) ignoring capitals and spaces is saved in that term's spelling: "net 10", "NET10" and "Net 10" all save as the shop's "Net 10". This applies to customers and vendors created or updated by an import, and created or updated through the Public API.”
  • Key Decisions: “Imports and the Public API stay lenient. A blank term gets the default; a name matching any of the shop's terms (standard or its own, active or deactivated, ignoring capitals and spaces) is saved as that term in its correct spelling, and a deactivated one then shows as "{name} (Inactive)"; any other text is saved as sent and dated as today.”
  • Assumptions: “Stored customer and vendor terms carry inconsistent spellings from old imports and migrations (for example "NET 30" and "Due On Receipt"); every count, match and move treats names as equal when they differ only in capitals and spaces.”
